To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
search engine marketing is a new paradigm in branding that has to be taken into account by both marketers and researchers.
search engine marketing is a new form of branding that is based on four key concepts: thematic spatialization, temporal hierarchization, consumer promiscuousness, and the consumer as a brand creator.

the dynamics of virtual branding in the search economy remain poorly understood, and that even postmodern branding paradigms fail to take into consideration the search economy and the surge of search engine marketing technologies, which allow search engines to manipulate time, space and consumer-brand constructs in unprecedented ways.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What is the nature of the branding paradigm in a'search' economy? How does the 'constraint of the signifier' impact on brand management? How do marketers need to adapt their brand management strategies to the'search' paradigm?

the following: (1) how search engines are changing the way brands are managed and how consumers relate to them; (2) how search engines and their associated technologies are changing the way marketers manage brands; (3) how the 'constraint of the sign' is affecting branding; (4) how the'search' paradigm is changing the way consumers relate to brands; and (5) how the 'brand' paradigm is being challenged by the'search' and'search engine' economy.
how marketers can use search engines to their advantage, and what implications this has for branding and marketing in a postmodern world.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the branding paradigm is undergoing radical change and that this is not being adequately addressed in the literature.
the current branding paradigm is not postmodern but post-postmodern.
the'search' paradigm is a key driver in the evolution of the branding paradigm, and that the branding paradigm is evolving in a way that will be increasingly difficult to control by marketers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in a search economy, the brand is no longer a sign, it becomes a search engine.
in a postmodern paradigm, brands are not only created by consumers, but they are also created for them, and in the process of doing so, they are also manipulated by the search engines.

the 'constraint of semioticisation' has led to a new economy where search engines are able to manipulate the consumer-brand relationship in unprecedented ways, and where marketers need to develop new branding strategies to take advantage of these new opportunities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamics of branding in the new search economy are not yet fully understood, and that the branding paradigm has to be re-conceptualized.
branding in the search economy is not about the creation of brand equity but about the manipulation of brand meaning.

marketers must be prepared to engage with the new'search' economy, which is characterised by the constraint of signification, and that they must be prepared to re-evaluate their brand management paradigms in light of this new reality.
